content:
Apple must respond by Monday to a complaint filed by Epic Games with the Brazilian antitrust regulator. Epic accuses Apple of a restrictive reading of its obligations under a recent antitrust settlement concerning the Brazilian App Store. Here are the details.

Background

Two months ago, Apple announced that developers can now distribute apps via alternative app marketplaces in Brazil.

The change was part of a settlement resolving a years-long antitrust investigation triggered by a complaint from Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre over Apple App Store rules.

Under the new terms, developers in Brazil can distribute iOS apps through alternative marketplaces and offer payment methods other than Apple's IAP system.

Apple also introduced a new commission structure, including a 5% Core Technology Fee on sales of digital goods and services inside apps distributed outside the App Store. Click here for more details on the structure.

Epic challenges Apple's implementation

According to Brazil's O Globo (citing MacMagazine) today, Epic recently filed a petition with Brazilian antitrust regulator CADE, accusing Apple of erecting "structural, technical and access barriers" that undermine the practical feasibility of alternative app distribution.

Epic says that while the new Brazilian terms apply only to iOS apps, Apple's agreement with CADE "expressly covers iPadOS."

The company reportedly also objects to so-called "scare screens," saying they discourage users from installing apps from outside the App Store. Epic also criticizes the current installation flow, saying it requires nine steps—three more than Apple's current setup in Europe.

O Globo reports that Epic added that Apple's original installation flow in Europe required 15 steps, but after being forced to reduce it to six, the "download abandonment rate fell from 65% to 25%."

Finally, Epic told CADE that Apple's reporting requirements "far exceed what is necessary to calculate the fee," allowing it to "monitor competitors' business models."

O Globo reports that CADE has given Apple until Monday to submit a response. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
